# CSX Reports Q3 2026 Revenue $4.02B; Operating Income $1.57B, EPS $0.57
CSX

CSX reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $4.02 billion and net earnings of $1.05 billion, or $0.57 per diluted share. Operating income for the quarter was $1.57 billion, a 44% increase year-over-year, and operating margin expanded to 39.1%.

seltz.snippet:
## CSX Earnings: 54% EPS Growth Masks Emerging Operational Headwinds

## Summary

CSX reported a strong financial quarter, with net earnings rising 52% to $1.05 billion and diluted EPS climbing 54% to $0.57 per share. Revenue increased 12% as total volume grew 5% to 1.69 million units. The company achieved an operating margin of 39.1%, an expansion of 8.8 percentage points year-over-year, demonstrating effective cost control and pricing leverage.

Despite financial outperformance, operational indicators signal potential headwinds. Network dwell time increased 12% and network velocity fell 2%, while intermodal trip plan performance declined 11%. These metrics are critical leading indicators for service quality; if service levels do not stabilize, the company may face risks to volume retention and pricing power, particularly as intermodal competition intensifies.

Fuel expenses added pressure, with locomotive fuel prices rising 67% year-over-year. While railroads often mitigate this volatility through surcharges, these mechanisms can introduce timing mismatches in margin recognition. The company’s ability to sustain 39% margins will depend on its success in normalizing network flow and offsetting energy costs.

Capital allocation remains a priority. With the completion of the Blue Ridge subdivision rebuild lowering the CAPEX burden, the company increased its dividend by 8% and authorized $5 billion in new share repurchases, with $5.2 billion remaining in total authorization. Management’s commitment to these returns suggests confidence in free cash flow, though the focus on immediate shareholder returns leaves less capital for near-term network capacity expansion.

Beyond operational metrics, the company maintains contingent liabilities regarding the Lower Passaic River. CSX is defending and indemnifying Pharmacia for legacy environmental liabilities, an obligation involving ongoing lawsuits and evolving consent

GAAP net earnings were $1,052 million (up 52% YoY), reflecting the quarter’s higher operating income. Operationally, intermodal revenue of $634 million rose 20% YoY, reflecting domestic shipment gains due to wins with key customers, new service offerings, and a tightening truck environment, while international shipments decreased slightly. Chemicals revenue of $790 million increased 13% YoY, driven primarily by higher shipments of petcoke, waste, plastics, and crude oil, and coal revenue of $537 million increased 10% YoY, reflecting higher export shipments of metallurgical and thermal coal due to increased production from re-opened mines, partially offset by lower domestic coal shipments to utility plants.
